edges.description: Supplying wild-type NDUFA2 to the patient's own cells restores what the variant took away, which is the standard demonstration that a candidate variant is causal.
edges.limitations: The rescue is partial rather than complete, and the reason is not resolved - transduction efficiency, expression level and the possibility of an irreversible component are all consistent with the result. The system is a patient fibroblast, so it says nothing about brain or heart, and only the null allele has been tested; the three missense patients have had no complementation experiment. Baculovirus-driven expression is also non-physiological in level and timing.

nodes.description: The rescue experiment from the founding study. Patient fibroblasts carrying the homozygous splice allele were transduced with a baculovirus expressing wild-type NDUFA2, and complex I expression, complex I activity and the mitochondrial membrane potential all improved. The rescue is described as partial, which the entry keeps - complementation establishes causality without establishing that the defect is fully correctable.

Two damaged copies of NDUFA2. Four patients and four alleles are known and they fall into two classes. The founding case is homozygous for the splice variant c.208+5G>A, which causes most transcripts to skip exon 2 with a frameshift; no protein or transcript was detected, so it behaves as a null. The three later patients carry missense alleles at residues that contact NDUFS1 - p.Lys45Thr, homozygous in one and in trans with the frameshift p.Asn76Metfs*4 in another, and p.Glu57Ala homozygous in the fourth.

nodes.description: The tissues that fail are the ones with the least metabolic reserve. In the founding patient this was brain and heart - Leigh disease with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, ending in cardiovascular arrest before the age of one. In the three later patients it was brain alone, presenting as white matter disease rather than as the symmetrical brainstem and basal ganglia lesions of Leigh syndrome. Which of the two patterns a patient gets is unexplained, and the correlation with allele class is discussed rather than asserted.

nodes.description: NDUFA2 binds the matrix arm through a single interface. It has exclusive contacts with the core subunit NDUFS1, made mostly through the flat four-stranded beta-sheet of its thioredoxin-like fold, and it sits at least 40 angstroms from any iron-sulfur cluster - so it cannot be doing chemistry, and what it can be doing is holding NDUFS1 in place. Both patient missense residues map to that interface: Lys45 contacts several NDUFS1 residues directly, and Glu57 makes a probable ion pair with NDUFS1 Arg382. The reading is that these alleles weaken the contact rather than remove the protein.

nodes.description: Losing NDUFA2 does not just weaken complex I, it prevents part of it from being built. In knockout cell lines, blue native electrophoresis shows the N-module only partly assembled, with the core subunits NDUFS1, NDUFV1 and NDUFV2 lost along with the accessory subunits NDUFS4, NDUFS6, NDUFA7 and NDUFV3. The N-module carries the NADH binding site, which is why activity falls further than the amount of residual complex would suggest. In the founding patient the same effect was described as disturbed assembly of complex I.

nodes.description: The measured biochemical endpoint, and the phenotype the entity is named for. The founding patient's deficiency was expressed in both skin fibroblasts and muscle, and it was isolated - the other respiratory chain complexes were spared, which is what a subunit dedicated to complex I predicts and what distinguishes this from the combined deficiencies caused by defects of mitochondrial gene expression. Transducing the patient's cells with a baculovirus expressing wild-type NDUFA2 partially restored complex I expression and activity, which is the experiment that makes the gene causal rather than merely associated.

nodes.description: The consequence measured in the founding patient's fibroblasts. Complex I is one of the proton pumps that build the inner membrane potential, so an enzyme that cannot oxidise NADH cannot pump, and the membrane depolarises. The depolarisation was corrected along with the enzyme when wild-type NDUFA2 was supplied, which ties it to the genotype rather than to the culture.
